title: BSC vs. Clean Bench Safety Distinction

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: A safety-focused restatement of the BSC vs. Clean Bench concept: never substitute a laminar flow clean bench for a biological safety cabinet when working with infectious material.
explanation: Because a clean bench and a Class II BSC can look similar, mistaking one for the other is a real and documented safety hazard — a clean bench's outward airflow (designed to protect the product) actively blows any aerosolized contaminant toward the worker's face, rather than away from it as a BSC's inward airflow does.
keyPractices: Confirm which type of cabinet is installed (check labeling/certification, not just appearance) before using it for infectious material.
Use only a certified, properly maintained biological safety cabinet of the appropriate class for infectious agent work.
Never use a laminar flow clean bench for infectious material, regardless of convenience.
